entities.name: Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji)
entities.label: Text
entities.summary:
A monumental work of Chinese historiography by Sima Qian (c. 145–86 BCE), covering over 2,000 years of Chinese history from the legendary Yellow Emperor to Emperor Wu of Han in 130 chapters (approximately 526,500 characters). The Shiji established the format for all subsequent Chinese dynastic histories: Basic Annals (benji, imperial chronology), Chronological Tables (biao), Treatises (shu, on topics like rites, music, astronomy, economics), Hereditary Houses (shijia, noble families), and Biographies (liezhuan, including foreign peoples).

Sima Qian completed this work despite being sentenced to castration by Emperor Wu for defending a disgraced general — a personal trauma he channeled into uncompromising historical honesty. The Shiji is not merely a chronicle but a work of literary art, with vivid character portraits, dramatic narrative, and moral commentary that set the standard for Chinese historical writing for 2,000 years.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: The Records of the Grand Historian (Shiji) is a foundational text in Chinese historiography that shaped the imperial chronology and established the format for subsequent dynastic histories. Its uncompromising historical honesty, despite Sima Qian's personal trauma, has had lasting regional significance.
